newsitem.title: USA: Viacom expects $300 million charge for Blockbuster. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Viacom expects $300 million charge for Blockbuster. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]

text.p: Viacom Inc. said on Tuesday that its Blockbuster unit's second-quarter financial results will be below Wall Street estimates and it will take a $300 million charge to reduce inventory and close underperforming stores.

Viacom, which said the rest of its businesses continued to perform well, said Blockbuster's second-quarter cash flow -- earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA -- was expected to be between $40 million and $50 million before charges.
For all of last year the video rental unit generated cash flow of about $687 million (corrects from $800 million).

The New York City-based company said that if Blockbuster's negative same-store sales trend continues into the second half, revenue shortfalls could result in full-year EBITDA between $400 million and $500 million.

Viacom said Blockbuster's revenues were affected by its headquarters move to Dallas, the effects of its changeover to self-distribution, the negative impact of a discontinued advertising campaign and the company's change in focus from video rental to an expanded retail product mix along with related store format changes.
It also cited cost pressures stemming from new store development and the "depth" of buying videotapes and other product, which it said resulted in excess inventory.

Viacom said the $300 million charges it will take in the second quarter were associated primarily with the reduction of carrying value of excess inventory and the closing of underperforming stores in certain international markets.
It said no domestic stores would be closed.

The company -- which also owns MTV Networks, Paramount Pictures, Showtime Networks, and publisher Simon & Schuster -- added that it had taken steps to address the operational issues affecting Blockbuster, including changes in its distribution system and a new advertising campaign.

It added that it believes Blockbuster, under John Antioco, the unit's new chairman, will improve performance by growing market share in the video rental category through improved marketing and promotion, better store site selection, more targeted tape purchases and a renewed emphasis on operational efficiency and customer service.

Viacom's stock, whose trading on the American Stock Exchanged was halted for almost two hours, fell after the news. The A shares fell by 62.5 cents to $28.8125 while the B shares lost 87.5 cents to $29.125.
